MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 22, 2021
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:00 p.m., on June 22, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on June 17, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Member Bucknum
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Stein Mart Property 25282 Marguerite
  Parkway; Agency Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, Keith Rattay, Elaine Lister, Cheryl
  Dyas and William Curley. Negotiating Party: Kinstler Family Trust. Under Negotiation-
  Price and Terms

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  June 22, 2021
 INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

P2. Cox Communication Services Update

  Communications. .

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Gabriel El Mahrek, M.V.: Expressed his opinion on the LGBTQ+ and outlined his thoughts.

Kathleen Cunningham, M.V.: Announced that the Friends of the Mission Viejo Library Bookstore
is now open and the grand re-opening today was a huge success. She announced that they will be
accepting used books starting August 2.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Inquired when the City is going to decide on the 2022 Elections. He indicated
that it is time to move forward with District based elections, so that residents can be informed.

Steve Bell, San Clemente: Stated that on June 9, 2019 Relay for Life raised over $215,000 to support
the American Cancer Society. Voiced concerns with the last year of less donations to the American
Cancer Society and a short-fall of $250 million due to the fact on not being able to hold the event
this past year. He announced that the Relay for Life of South Orange County will take place on the
Village Green on August 28 from 2:00 to 10:00 p.m.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Ms. Schlicht played an audio clip from Council Member Sachs Council
Comments from the May 25, 2021 City Council Meeting. She stated that this was a Brown Act
Violation. She accused Mayor Kelley and Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum of colluding with Council
Member Sachs to publicly shame and blind side the Capistrano School District with a list of their
grievances. She outlined her reasons there was a Brown Act Violation. She questioned the City’s
Legal Department expenses and she believes the change in these expenses was due to the California
Voters Rights Act Lawsuit that should have been prevented

Mark Neely, M.V.: Stated he agreed with Mr. Lawson’s statement that there are some crazy things
going on with the Council. He agrees with affordable housing in Mission Viejo. Asked what
Council is doing on the affordable housing.

Andrea Alexander, Lake Forest: Voiced concern with the fact that the City has not gone to District
Elections. She explained the process that the City of Lake Forest went through to convert to district
voting and spoke about the benefits within the City of Lake Forest.

37. Preliminary Consideration of Draft Update to the City of Mission Viejo General Plan
  Housing Element for the 2021-2029 Planning Period Pursuant to the Requirements of
  State Law (Continued from the 6/08/21 City Council Meeting)

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister and Planning and Economic Development
  Manager Larry Longenecker presented the staff report.

  Randall Simmons, M.V.: Asked that the City Council find building sites for affordable
  housing and that 15% of the units be designated for low and very low-income wage earners.
  Questioned why the city does not have an Ordinance stipulating this.

  Sally Simmons, M.V.: Spoke in favor of affordable housing for wage earners making less
  than $50k annually. Stated that she is favor of mixed use with both affordable housing and
  businesses at failing strip malls.

  Ann Owens, Lake Forest: Stated that Site C should be eliminated as a viable site. Voiced
  concerns that unless there is a policy mandating 15% of any future housing be designated for
  low to very-low income, any developer can take over that land and build whatever they
  choose.

  Ilene Giger, M.V.: Advocated for the development of 1,075 affordable housing units per the
  RHNA. Voiced concerns on the financial viability of Site C and the freeway corridor.
  Encouraged the Council to invest in these sites to ensure they are financially viable for
  affordable housing.

  Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Asked that the City Council adopt an inclusionary housing policy that
  requires all new housing units built in the city to be affordable for those earning $50k or less
  annually. Stated that of all the available sites, the Big Lots to Del Taco Strip Mall is most
  appropriate for mixed-use zoning. She felt that the City lacked transparency and opportunity
  for public input on this item.

  Jon Achee, M.V.: Asked that the Council look at affordable housing for young families and
  essential workers to revitalize our community.

  Sue Johnson, M.V.: Pointed out to the Council the rents in Orange County keep rising and
  encouraged the Council to entice developers to build affordable housing. Stated that 91% of
  the workforce in the City live elsewhere.

City Council Minutes  9  June 22, 2021
   Michael Schlesinger, M.V. Questioned why the City has so few affordable housing units.

  Linda Tang, M.V.: Outlined her ideas for consideration as the City drafts the 2021-29

 43. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell gave a shout-out to the Mission Viejo Nadadores who just completed the
Olympic Swimming and Diving Trials in Omaha, Nebraska. He announced that four Nadadore
Swimmers will be on the U.S. Olympic Swim Team: Haley Anderson, Open Water Swim; Michael
Brinegar, 800 and 1500-meter Freestyle Swim; Zach Apple, 4 by 100-meter Freestyle Relay Swim;
and Annie Lazor, 200- meter breaststroke swim.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked Cox Communications for their presentation this evening.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs stated the survey that was initially taken showed that the majority of
Mission Viejo Voters wanted to keep at-large voting. He feels that Mission Viejo is one of the
leaders in regards to respect for our businesses. He heard that San Clemente is charging $100 per
parking spot to the restaurants that have used public road ways to expand their businesses during
COVID. He let the City Council know that he worked on a resolution with the City Attorney and
City Manager in which in essence states that we love our businesses and want to protect them and
keep working for them. He reminded residents that the City Council voted 5-0 to give over a million
dollars in grants to our businesses to help keep them open during the pandemic. He asked the City
Council to review and comment if necessary to the City Attorney on the resolution that he will bring
iback at the next council meeting. Lastly, he stated that he is on the Board of the Pacific Symphony
and the Gala Fundraiser this past Saturday raised $2.2mm which is the highest amount raised in the
history of the Gala performance.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum gave a shout out to the Pacific Symphony on the Gala fundraiser that
was held on the Village Green this past Saturday. She commented on the decorations. Mayor Pro
Tem stated she is looking forward to the Pacific Symphony Event on August 14. She thanked
Steve Bell on his work with Relay for Life. She reiterated that the City has held public forums on
Districting in the past. Lastly, she wished everyone a Happy Independence Day and asked everyone
to be considerate with parking.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley stated she also attended the Gala and is glad to hear how much money was raised
and look forward to attending the next event on August 14. She attended the South Mission Viejo
Little League closing ceremony and it was great to see all the kids. Lastly, she wished all the
students to have a safe summer.
